title: WHEN: A Wavelet-DTW Hybrid Attention Network for Heterogeneous Time Series Analysis

problem.claim: Time series analysis is challenging, particularly when multiple time series exhibit intra-sequence non-stationarity and inter-sequence asynchronism.

gap.claim: Existing deep learning methods have not adequately addressed heterogeneity in time series.

contributions.claim: The authors propose WHEN, a hybrid attention network for heterogeneous time series classification and forecasting.
WaveAtt integrates a data-dependent wavelet function into a BiLSTM network to analyze dynamic frequency components in nonstationary time series.
DTWAtt converts dynamic time warping into an attention mechanism that synchronizes input sequences with a universal parameter sequence.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the data-dependent wavelet function as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on 30 UEA datasets and 3 real-world datasets with competitive baselines are reported to demonstrate excellent model performance.
A specially designed analysis is reported to explore WHEN's ability to handle time series heterogeneities.

narrative_sequence.summary: Time series analysis is broadly useful but remains challenging.
Deep learning has succeeded in time series tasks, but heterogeneity—especially non-stationarity and asynchronism—remains inadequately addressed.
WHEN combines WaveAtt and DTWAtt to model dynamic frequency variation and cross-sequence time distortion.
The hybrid-attention network is formulated for classification or forecasting according to the task.
The authors report benchmark experiments and targeted heterogeneity analysis.

unknowns: Quantitative results, evaluation metrics, and statistical comparisons are not provided.
Dataset characteristics, baseline identities, training details, and ablation results are not provided.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
